title.zh: 卷2 帝紀第2 文帝下
title.raw: 卷2 帝紀第2 文帝下 Volume 2 Annals 2: Emperor Wen 2

sentences.zh: 文帝下

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Wen, Part Two

sentences.zh: 魏大統元年春正月己酉，進太祖督中外諸軍事、錄尚書事、大行臺，改封安定郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Western Wei Datong, spring, first month, day jiyou, the Grand Duke was advanced to supervise all military affairs at home and abroad, Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Commissioner-in-Chief; his fief was changed to Duke of Anding commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Datong (535), on the jiyou day of the first month, Yuwen Tai was promoted to supervise all armies at home and abroad, made recorder of the Masters of Writing, and grand commissioner-in-chief, and enfeoffed as duke of Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 太祖固讓王及錄尚書事，魏帝許之，乃改封安定郡公。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke firmly declined the kingship and the post of recorder; the Wei emperor granted this, and he was thereupon re-enfeoffed as Duke of Anding commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai firmly declined both the royal title and the recordership; the Wei emperor assented, and he was re-enfeoffed as duke of Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣其將司馬子如寇潼關，太祖軍霸上，子如乃回軍自蒲津寇華州，刺史王羆擊走之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent its general Sima Ziru to raid Tong Pass; the Grand Duke encamped at Bashang. Ziru then turned his army back from Pujin to raid Hua Province; the governor Wang Pi drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Sima Ziru against Tong Pass; Yuwen Tai camped at Bashang. Ziru doubled back from Pujin to strike Hua Province, but Governor Wang Pi repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 三月，太祖以戎役屢興，民吏勞弊，乃命所司斟酌今古，參考變通，可以益國利民便時適治者，為二十四條新制，奏魏帝行之。

translations.literal: In the third month, because military campaigns had been raised repeatedly and officials and people were worn with toil, the Grand Duke ordered the relevant offices to weigh past and present, consult changes and adaptations, and wherever something could benefit the state, profit the people, and suit the times and good government, frame twenty-four articles of new institutions, present them to the Wei emperor, and put them into effect.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, seeing repeated campaigns and exhausted officials and people, Yuwen Tai ordered the ministries to draw on past and present practice and draft twenty-four new statutes that would strengthen the state, ease the people, and fit the times; he submitted them to the Wei emperor for enactment.

sentences.zh: 二年春三月，東魏襲陷夏州，留其將張瓊、許和守之。

translations.literal: In the second year, spring, third month, Eastern Wei made a surprise attack and seized Xia Province, leaving its generals Zhang Qiong and Xu He to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year, third month, Eastern Wei seized Xia Province by surprise and left Zhang Qiong and Xu He to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，秦州刺史、建中王万俟普撥率所部叛入東魏。

translations.literal: In summer, fifth month, the governor of Qin Province, Prince Jianzhong Wan'niu Puba, led his command in rebellion into Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, Wan'niu Puba, Prince Jianzhong and governor of Qin Province, defected with his troops to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 太祖勒輕騎追之，至河北千餘里，不及而還。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke led light cavalry in pursuit, reaching more than a thousand li north of the river, but failed to overtake him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai pursued with light cavalry for over a thousand li north of the Yellow River, failed to catch him, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月，東魏寇龍門，屯軍蒲阪，造三道浮橋度河。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, first month, Eastern Wei raided Longmen, encamped at Puban, and built three pontoon bridges to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the third year, first month, Eastern Wei attacked Longmen, camped at Puban, and threw three pontoon bridges across the river.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將竇泰趣潼關，高敖曹圍洛州。

translations.literal: They also sent their general Dou Tai toward Tong Pass, while Gao Aocao besieged Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: They sent Dou Tai toward Tong Pass and Gao Aocao to besiege Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 太祖出軍廣陽，召諸將曰：「賊今掎吾三面，又造橋於河，示欲必渡，是欲綴吾軍，使竇泰得西入耳。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke led the army out from Guangyang and summoned the generals, saying: "The enemy now grips us on three sides and has built bridges on the river, showing that they mean surely to cross—this is to pin our army so that Dou Tai can slip west.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai marched from Guangyang and told his generals: "The foe has us pinned on three sides and bridged the river as if to force a crossing—they mean to hold us here while Dou Tai slips through to the west.

sentences.zh: 久與相持，其計得行，非良策也。

translations.literal: To stay locked with them long and let their plan succeed is no good stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: A long standoff that lets them carry out that plan is poor strategy.

sentences.zh: 且歡起兵以來，泰每為先驅，其下多銳卒，屢勝而驕。

translations.literal: Moreover, since Huan raised his army, Tai has always led the van; his troops are mostly crack soldiers, and repeated victories have made them arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, since Huan took the field Dou Tai has always spearheaded his attacks with elite troops grown arrogant from many victories.

sentences.zh: 今出其不意，襲之必克。

translations.literal: Strike them now where they do not expect it and you are sure to win.
translations.idiomatic: Hit them unexpectedly now and victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 克泰則歡不戰而自走矣。

translations.literal: If Tai is taken, Huan will withdraw without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Capture Dou Tai and Huan will retreat without a battle.

sentences.zh: 」諸將咸曰：「賊在近，捨而遠襲，事若蹉跌，悔無及也。

translations.literal: " All the generals said: "The enemy is near; to abandon them and strike far off—if the affair should slip, regret will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: " The generals objected: "The enemy is close; to leave them and strike elsewhere risks disaster we cannot undo.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「歡前再襲潼關，吾軍不過霸上。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke said: "When Huan twice raided Tong Pass before, our army never went beyond Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai replied: "When Huan attacked Tong Pass twice before, we never marched past Bashang.

sentences.zh: 今者大來，兵未出郊。

translations.literal: Now he comes in force, yet his troops have not left the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Now he comes in strength, but his army has not even cleared the outskirts.

sentences.zh: 賊顧謂吾但自守耳，無遠鬥意。

translations.literal: The enemy thinks we mean only to hold our ground and have no mind to fight far off.
translations.idiomatic: They take us for mere defenders with no appetite for a distant battle.

sentences.zh: 又狃于得志，有輕我之心。

translations.literal: They are also emboldened by success and look down on us.
translations.idiomatic: Success has made them overconfident and contemptuous of us.

sentences.zh: 乘此擊之，何往不克。

translations.literal: Strike them in this mood and where will you not prevail?
translations.idiomatic: Strike while they feel this way and where will you fail?

sentences.zh: 賊雖造橋，不能徑渡。

translations.literal: Though the enemy has built bridges, they cannot cross straight over.
translations.idiomatic: Their bridges cannot carry them across at once.

sentences.zh: 此五日中，吾取竇泰必矣。

translations.literal: Within these five days I shall take Dou Tai for certain.
translations.idiomatic: Within five days I will surely take Dou Tai.

sentences.zh: 公等勿疑。

translations.literal: You gentlemen need not doubt it.
translations.idiomatic: Have no doubts.

sentences.zh: 」庚戌，太祖率騎六千還長安，聲言欲保隴右。

translations.literal: On day gengxu the Grand Duke led six thousand horsemen back to Chang'an, publicly announcing that he meant to secure Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day Yuwen Tai led six thousand cavalry back to Chang'an, proclaiming that he would secure Longyou.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，謁帝而潛出軍。

translations.literal: On day xinhai he paid court to the emperor and secretly marched out.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he attended court, then slipped out with the army.

sentences.zh: 癸丑旦，至小關。

translations.literal: At dawn on day guichou he reached Xiaoguan.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on guichou day he reached Xiaoguan Pass.

sentences.zh: 竇泰卒聞軍至，惶懼，依山為陣，未及成列，太祖縱兵擊破之，盡俘其衆萬餘人。

translations.literal: Dou Tai's troops, hearing the army had arrived, were panic-stricken; they drew up on the mountain before ranks could be formed, and the Grand Duke loosed his soldiers, broke them, and took more than ten thousand alive.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tai's men, hearing he had come, panicked and formed on the slopes before their lines were set; Yuwen Tai attacked, routed them, and captured more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 斬泰，傳首長安。

translations.literal: Dou Tai was beheaded and his head sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Tai was killed and his head sent to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高敖曹適陷洛州，執刺史泉企，聞泰之歿，焚輜重棄城走。

translations.literal: Gao Aocao had just taken Luo Province and seized the governor Quan Qi; hearing of Tai's death he burned the baggage train and abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Aocao had just captured Luo Province and taken Governor Quan Qi; when he heard Dou Tai was dead he burned his wagons and fled.

sentences.zh: 齊神武亦撤橋而退。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu also withdrew his bridges and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu (Gao Huan) likewise pulled back his bridges and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 企子元禮尋復洛州，斬東魏刺史杜密。

translations.literal: Qi's son Yuanli soon recovered Luo Province and beheaded the Eastern Wei governor Du Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Qi's son Yuanli soon retook Luo Province and killed the Eastern Wei governor Du Mi.

sentences.zh: 太祖還軍長安。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke returned the army to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai marched back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 六月，遣儀同于謹取楊氏壁。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he sent the army comrade Yu Jin to take Yangshi rampart.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he sent Army Comrade Yu Jin to seize Yangshi fortress.

sentences.zh: 太祖請罷行臺，帝復申前命，太祖受錄尚書事，餘固讓，乃止。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke requested that the Grand Commissionerate be abolished; the emperor renewed his earlier command, the Grand Duke accepted the recordership of the Masters of Writing, but firmly declined the rest and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai asked to abolish the grand commissionerate; the emperor repeated his earlier appointment, and Yuwen Tai accepted the recordership but declined the rest, and so it ended.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，徵兵會咸陽。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, troops were levied to assemble at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn levies were called to assemble at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 八月丁丑，太祖率李弼、獨孤信、梁禦、趙貴、于謹、若干惠、怡峯、劉亮、王德、侯莫陳崇、李遠、達奚武等十二將東伐。

translations.literal: On the eighth month, day dingchou, the Grand Duke led Li Bi, Dugu Xin, Liang Yu, Zhao Gui, Yu Jin, Ruogan Hui, Yi Feng, Liu Liang, Wang De, Houmochen Chong, Li Yuan, Daxi Wu, and eleven other generals east on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day of the eighth month Yuwen Tai marched east with Li Bi, Dugu Xin, Liang Yu, Zhao Gui, Yu Jin, Ruogan Hui, Yi Feng, Liu Liang, Wang De, Houmochen Chong, Li Yuan, Daxi Wu, and eleven other commanders.

sentences.zh: 至潼關，太祖乃誓於師曰：「與爾有衆，奉天威，誅暴亂。

translations.literal: Reaching Tong Pass, the Grand Duke then swore to the army: "With you I have a host; by Heaven's majesty we punish violence and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass Yuwen Tai swore to the troops: "With you I have an army; by Heaven's mandate we punish the violent and rebellious.

sentences.zh: 惟爾士，整爾甲兵，戒爾戎事，無貪財以輕敵，無暴民以作威。

translations.literal: You soldiers—array your armor and arms, ready your martial tasks; do not covet spoils and so slight the enemy, do not brutalize the people and so make a tyrant's show.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers, brace your arms and gear and keep discipline: do not grasp at loot and underestimate the foe, do not terrorize the people to play the despot.

sentences.zh: 用命則有賞，不用命則有戮。

translations.literal: Obey orders and there are rewards; disobey orders and there is execution.
translations.idiomatic: Obey and you will be rewarded; disobey and you will be punished.

sentences.zh: 爾衆士其勉之。

translations.literal: You host of soldiers, exert yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: All of you, strive hard.

sentences.zh: 」遣于謹居軍前，狥地至盤豆。

translations.literal: He sent Yu Jin to lead the van and pacify the countryside as far as Pandou.
translations.idiomatic: He put Yu Jin in the van to clear the route as far as Pandou.

sentences.zh: 東魏將高叔禮守柵不下，謹急攻之，乃降。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei general Gao Shuli held a palisade and would not yield; Jin pressed the attack hotly and he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei's Gao Shuli held a stockade and refused to submit; Jin stormed it until he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 獲其戍卒一千，送叔禮於長安。

translations.literal: They took a thousand garrison soldiers and sent Shuli to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand garrison troops were captured and Shuli was sent to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 戊子，至弘農。

translations.literal: On day wuzi they reached Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day they reached Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 東魏將高干、陝州刺史李徽伯拒守。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei generals Gao Gan and the governor of Shaan Province Li Huibo held the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei's Gao Gan and Shaan governor Li Huibo defended the city.

sentences.zh: 于時連雨，太祖乃命諸軍冒雨攻之。

translations.literal: Rain fell in succession; the Grand Duke then ordered the armies to attack in the rain.
translations.idiomatic: Steady rain fell; Yuwen Tai ordered an assault through the downpour.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，城潰，斬徽伯，虜其戰士八千。

translations.literal: On day gengyin the walls collapsed; Huibo was beheaded and eight thousand fighting men were captured.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day the walls gave way; Li Huibo was killed and eight thousand soldiers taken.

sentences.zh: 高干走度河，令賀拔勝追擒之，並送長安。

translations.literal: Gao Gan fled across the river; the Grand Duke ordered Helba Sheng to pursue and seize him, and both were sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gan fled across the river; Yuwen Tai sent Helba Sheng in pursuit to capture him, and both prisoners were sent to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 於是宜陽、邵郡皆來歸附。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yiyang and Shao commandery both came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang and Shao commandery then submitted.

sentences.zh: 先是河南豪傑多聚兵應東魏，至是各率所部來降。

translations.literal: Earlier many magnates south of the river had raised troops in support of Eastern Wei; now each led his following to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Many Henan strongmen who had backed Eastern Wei now brought their bands over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 齊神武懼，率衆十萬出壺口，趨蒲阪，將自后土濟。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu was afraid and led a host of a hundred thousand out of Hukou toward Puban, intending to cross from Houtu.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu, alarmed, marched a hundred thousand men from Hukou toward Puban to cross at Houtu ford.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將高敖曹以三萬人出河南。

translations.literal: He also sent his general Gao Aocao with thirty thousand men out on the Henan route.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Gao Aocao with thirty thousand down the Henan line.

sentences.zh: 是歲，關中饑。

translations.literal: That year Guanzhong suffered famine.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong suffered famine that year.

sentences.zh: 太祖旣平弘農，因館谷五十餘日。

translations.literal: After the Grand Duke had pacified Hongnong he quartered on stored grain for more than fifty days.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Hongnong Yuwen Tai lived on local grain stores for more than fifty days.

sentences.zh: 時戰士不滿萬人，聞齊神武將度，乃引軍入關。

translations.literal: At the time the fighting men numbered fewer than ten thousand; hearing that Qi Shenwu was about to cross, he then led the army into the passes.
translations.idiomatic: His active troops numbered fewer than ten thousand; when he heard Qi Shenwu was crossing, he withdrew into the passes.

sentences.zh: 齊神武遂度河，逼華州。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu thereupon crossed the river and pressed Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu crossed the river and advanced on Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 刺史王羆嚴守。

translations.literal: The governor Wang Pi held a strict defense.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Pi defended stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 知不可攻，乃涉洛，軍于許原西。

translations.literal: Seeing that it could not be taken, he then crossed the Luo and encamped west of Xuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the city untakable, he crossed the Luo and camped west of Xuyuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖據渭南，徵諸州兵皆〔未〕會。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke held the south bank of the Wei; levies from the provinces had not yet assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai held the south bank of the Wei River while provincial levies had not yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 乃召諸將謂之曰：「高歡越山度河，遠來至此，天亡之時也。

translations.literal: He then summoned the generals and said to them: "Gao Huan has crossed mountains and rivers and come from afar—this is the hour Heaven destroys him.
translations.idiomatic: He called his generals and said: "Gao Huan has crossed mountains and rivers to reach us—Heaven's moment to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 吾欲擊之何如？

translations.literal: I wish to strike him—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to attack—what say you?

sentences.zh: 」諸將咸以衆寡不敵，請待歡更西，以觀其勢。

translations.literal: " All the generals, citing inferior numbers, asked to wait until Huan advanced further west and watch how matters developed.
translations.idiomatic: " They pleaded inferior numbers and asked to let Huan push farther west before judging the situation.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「歡若得至咸陽，人情轉騷擾。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke said: "If Huan reaches Xianyang the people's hearts will turn to turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai said: "If Huan reaches Xianyang the realm will panic.

sentences.zh: 今及其新至，便可擊之。

translations.literal: Now, while he is newly arrived, we can strike at once.
translations.idiomatic: Strike now, while he has just arrived.

sentences.zh: 」即造浮橋於渭，令軍人齎三日糧，輕騎度渭，輜重自渭南夾渭而西。

translations.literal: " He immediately built pontoon bridges on the Wei, ordered the soldiers to carry three days' grain, and led light cavalry across the Wei; baggage and heavy train went west along both banks of the Wei from the south shore.
translations.idiomatic: " He threw pontoon bridges on the Wei, gave each man three days' rations, crossed with light cavalry, and sent the baggage train west along both banks from the southern shore.

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬辰，至沙苑，距齊神武軍六十餘里。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, day renchen, they reached Shayuan, sixty-odd li from Qi Shenwu's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on renchen day, they reached Shayuan, a little over sixty li from Qi Shenwu's camp.

sentences.zh: 齊神武聞太祖至，引軍來會。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu, hearing the Grand Duke had arrived, led his army to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu, learning Yuwen Tai was there, marched to engage him.

sentences.zh: 癸巳旦，候騎告齊神武軍且至。

translations.literal: At dawn on day guisi the scouts reported that Qi Shenwu's army was approaching.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on guisi day scouts reported Qi Shenwu's host drawing near.

sentences.zh: 太祖召諸將謀之。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke summoned the generals to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai called a council of war.

sentences.zh: 李弼曰：「彼衆我寡，不可平地置陣。

translations.literal: Li Bi said: "They are many and we few—we cannot set battle lines on open ground.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi said: "They outnumber us; we cannot fight on flat ground.

sentences.zh: 此東十里有渭曲，可先據以待之。

translations.literal: Ten li east of here is a bend of the Wei—we should seize it first and wait there.
translations.idiomatic: Ten li east is a bend of the Wei—take it first and await them there.

sentences.zh: 」遂進軍至渭曲，背水東西為陣。

translations.literal: They advanced to the bend of the Wei and drew up facing the water, east and west.
translations.idiomatic: They moved to the river bend and formed lines with the water at their backs, east and west.

sentences.zh: 李弼為右拒，趙貴為左拒。

translations.literal: Li Bi held the right refusal; Zhao Gui the left refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi commanded the right wing; Zhao Gui the left.

sentences.zh: 命將士皆偃戈於葭蘆中，聞鼓聲而起。

translations.literal: He ordered officers and soldiers to lay their weapons in the reeds and rise at the sound of the drum.
translations.idiomatic: He hid the troops in the reeds with weapons down, to rise at the drum.

sentences.zh: 申時，齊神武至，望太祖軍少，競馳而進，不為行列，總萃於左軍。

translations.literal: At the shen hour Qi Shenwu arrived; seeing the Grand Duke's army few, all raced forward without forming ranks, massing on the left wing.
translations.idiomatic: At the shen hour Qi Shenwu came up; seeing few defenders, his men charged in disorder, crowding the left wing.

sentences.zh: 兵將交，太祖鳴鼓，士皆奮起。

translations.literal: As the armies met the Grand Duke sounded the drum and the soldiers all leapt up.
translations.idiomatic: As the lines met Yuwen Tai beat the drum and his men sprang up.

sentences.zh: 于謹等六軍與之合戰，李弼等率鐵騎橫擊之，絕其軍為二隊，大破之，斬六千餘級，臨陣降者二萬餘人。

translations.literal: Yu Jin's six armies joined battle with them; Li Bi and the others led armored cavalry in a flanking strike, cutting the enemy host in two, routing them utterly; more than six thousand were beheaded and over twenty thousand surrendered on the field.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin's six corps engaged them; Li Bi and others led iron cavalry in a flank attack, split the enemy in two, and crushed them—six thousand killed and twenty thousand surrendered on the spot.

sentences.zh: 齊神武夜遁，追至河上，復大克獲。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu fled by night; pursuing to the river they again won a great capture.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu fled by night; pursuit to the river yielded another great haul.

sentences.zh: 前後虜其卒七萬。

translations.literal: In all they captured seventy thousand of his soldiers before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Altogether they took seventy thousand prisoners in the campaign.

sentences.zh: 留其甲士二萬，餘悉縱歸。

translations.literal: They kept twenty thousand armored fighting men; the rest were all released to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand armored men were kept; the rest were sent home.

sentences.zh: 收其輜重兵甲，獻俘長安。

translations.literal: They gathered the baggage train, armor, and weapons and presented the captives in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Captured wagons, armor, and arms were brought in, and the prisoners displayed at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 還軍渭南，於是所徵諸州兵始至。

translations.literal: Returning the army to the south bank of the Wei, the levies from the provinces then arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Back on the south bank of the Wei, the provincial levies finally came in.

sentences.zh: 乃於戰所，准當時兵士，人種樹一株，以旌武功。

translations.literal: Thereupon at the battlefield, reckoning the soldiers of the time, each man planted one tree to commemorate the martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: At the battlefield each soldier of the day planted a tree to mark the victory.

sentences.zh: 進太祖柱國大將軍，增邑幷前五千戶。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke was advanced to pillar-of-state grand general; his fief was increased by five thousand households together with what he already held.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai was promoted to pillar-of-state grand general with five thousand additional households added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 李弼等十二將亦進爵增邑。

translations.literal: Li Bi and the other twelve generals also advanced in rank and had their fiefs increased.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi and the other twelve commanders were also promoted and enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 幷其下將士，賞各有差。

translations.literal: Together with the officers and soldiers beneath them, rewards were graded according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate officers and troops were rewarded according to merit.

sentences.zh: 遣左僕射、馮翊王元季海為行臺，與開府獨孤信率步騎二萬向洛陽；

translations.literal: He sent the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Fengyi Yuan Jihai, as commissioner-in-chief, and together with the grand marshal Dugu Xin led twenty thousand foot and horse toward Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Left Vice Director Yuan Jihai, Prince of Fengyi, as commissioner-in-chief, with Grand Marshal Dugu Xin and twenty thousand infantry and cavalry toward Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 洛州刺史李顯趨荊州；

translations.literal: the governor of Luo Province Li Xian hurried to Jing Province;
translations.idiomatic: Luo governor Li Xian fled toward Jing Province;

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝、李弼渡河圍蒲阪。

translations.literal: Helba Sheng and Li Bi crossed the river and besieged Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Helba Sheng and Li Bi crossed the river to besiege Puban.

sentences.zh: 牙門將高子信開門納勝軍，東魏將薛崇禮棄城走，勝等追獲之。

translations.literal: The gate officer Gao Zixin opened the gates and admitted Sheng's army; the Eastern Wei general Xue Chongli abandoned the city and fled, and Sheng and the others pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Gate officer Gao Zixin opened the gates to Sheng; Eastern Wei's Xue Chongli fled and was caught in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 太祖進軍蒲阪，略定汾、絳。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke advanced the army to Puban and pacified Fen and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai marched to Puban and secured Fen and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 於是許和殺張瓊以夏州降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xu He killed Zhang Qiong and surrendered Xia Province.
translations.idiomatic: Xu He then killed Zhang Qiong and surrendered Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖自弘農入關後，東魏將高敖曹圍弘農，聞其軍敗，退守洛陽。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the Grand Duke entered the passes from Hongnong, the Eastern Wei general Gao Aocao had besieged Hongnong; hearing of the army's defeat he withdrew to hold Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Tai entered the passes from Hongnong, Gao Aocao had besieged the city; when he heard of the defeat he fell back to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信至新安，敖曹復走度河，信遂入洛陽。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin reached Xin'an; Aocao again fled across the river, and Xin thereupon entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin reached Xin'an; Aocao fled across the river again, and Xin entered Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 東魏潁川長史賀若統與密縣人張儉執刺史田迅舉城降。

translations.literal: The Eastern Wei chief clerk of Yingchuan He Ruotong and Zhang Jian of Mi County seized the governor Tian Xun and raised the city in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei's Yingchuan chief clerk He Ruotong and Mi County's Zhang Jian arrested Governor Tian Xun and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 滎陽鄭榮業、鄭偉等攻梁州，擒其刺史鹿永吉；

translations.literal: Zheng Rongye and Zheng Wei of Xingyang attacked Liang Province and captured its governor Lu Yongji;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Rongye and Zheng Wei of Xingyang took Liang Province and captured Governor Lu Yongji;

sentences.zh: 清河人崔彥穆、檀琛攻滎陽，擒其郡守蘇定：皆來附。

translations.literal: Cui Yanmu of Qinghe and Tan Chen attacked Xingyang and captured the prefect Su Ding: all came to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanmu of Qinghe and Tan Chen took Xingyang and seized Prefect Su Ding—all submitted.

sentences.zh: 自梁、陳已西，將吏降者相屬。

translations.literal: From Liang and Chen westward, officials and generals who surrendered followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: West of Liang and Chen, surrendering officials and generals came in one after another.

sentences.zh: 於是東魏將堯雄、趙育、是云寶出潁川，欲復降地。

translations.literal: Thereupon Eastern Wei generals Yao Xiong, Zhao Yu, and Shi Yunbao came out of Yingchuan, wishing to recover the surrendered territory.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei then sent Yao Xiong, Zhao Yu, and Shi Yunbao out of Yingchuan to win back lost ground.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣儀同宇文貴、梁遷等逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke sent Army Comrade Yuwen Gui, Liang Qian, and others to meet and strike them, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai sent Army Comrade Yuwen Gui, Liang Qian, and others to intercept them and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 趙育來降。

translations.literal: Zhao Yu came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 東魏復遣將任祥率河南兵與雄合，儀同怡峯與貴、遷等復擊破之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei again sent the general Ren Xiang leading Henan troops to join with Xiong; Army Comrade Yiyi Feng together with Gui, Qian, and the others again struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Ren Xiang with Henan troops to reinforce Xiong; Yiyi Feng, Yuwen Gui, and Liang Qian defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 又遣都督韋孝寬取豫州。

translations.literal: He also sent Supervisor Wei Xiaokuan to take Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai also sent Supervisor Wei Xiaokuan to seize Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 是云寶殺其東揚州刺史那

translations.literal: Shi Yunbao killed the Eastern Yangzhou governor Na
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yunbao killed Eastern Yangzhou governor Na Chun (那/樁/椿) and surrendered the province.

translations.literal: (Chun 樁)
translations.idiomatic: (Chun 樁)

sentences.zh: 〔椿〕，以州來附。

translations.literal: (Chun 椿), and brought the province to submit.
translations.idiomatic: and brought the province over in submission.

sentences.zh: 四年春三月，太祖率諸將入朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, spring, third month, the Grand Duke led the generals to court.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fourth year, third month, Yuwen Tai led his commanders to court.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，還華州。

translations.literal: When the rites were finished, he returned to Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the audience ended, he returned to Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 七月，東魏遣其將侯景、厙狄干、高敖曹、

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Eastern Wei sent its generals Hou Jing, Kudigan Gan, Gao Aocao,
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Eastern Wei sent Hou Jing, Kudigan Gan, Gao Aocao,

translations.literal: (Yuan)
translations.idiomatic: (Yuan)

sentences.zh: 〔韓〕軌、可朱渾元、莫多婁貸文等圍獨孤信於洛陽。

translations.literal: Han Gui, Kezhuhun Yuan, Moduolou Daiwen, and others to besiege Dugu Xin at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gui, Kezhuhun Yuan, Moduolou Daiwen, and others to besiege Dugu Xin at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 齊神武繼其後。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu followed after them.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu (Gao Huan) followed in their wake.

sentences.zh: 先是，魏帝將幸洛陽拜園陵，會信被圍，詔太祖率軍救信，魏帝亦東。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Wei emperor had planned to visit Luoyang to pay respects at the imperial tombs; when Xin was besieged, he ordered the Grand Duke to lead troops to rescue Xin, and the Wei emperor also marched east.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor had been preparing to visit Luoyang and the imperial tombs; when Dugu Xin was trapped, he ordered Yuwen Tai to relieve him and marched east himself.

sentences.zh: 八月庚寅，太祖至穀城，莫多婁貸文、可朱渾元來逆，臨陣斬貸文，元單騎遁免，悉虜其衆送弘農。

translations.literal: On the eighth month, day gengyin, the Grand Duke reached Gucheng; Moduolou Daiwen and Kezhuhun Yuan came to meet him; Daiwen was beheaded in battle, Yuan fled alone on horseback and escaped, and all their troops were captured and sent to Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day of the eighth month Yuwen Tai reached Gucheng; Moduolou Daiwen and Kezhuhun Yuan came out to fight; Daiwen was killed in the clash, Yuan fled alone on horseback, and the whole force was taken and sent to Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 遂進軍瀍東。

translations.literal: Thereupon he advanced the army to the east of the Chan River.
translations.idiomatic: He then pushed east of the Chan River.

sentences.zh: 是夕，魏帝幸太祖營，於是景等夜解圍去。

translations.literal: That evening the Wei emperor visited the Grand Duke's camp; thereupon Jing and the others lifted the siege by night and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That night the Wei emperor came to Yuwen Tai's camp; Hou Jing and the others broke the siege and withdrew under cover of darkness.

sentences.zh: 及旦，太祖率輕騎追之，至於河上。

translations.literal: At dawn the Grand Duke led light cavalry in pursuit, reaching the river.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Yuwen Tai pursued with light cavalry as far as the river.

sentences.zh: 景等北據河橋，南屬邙山為陣，與諸軍合戰。

translations.literal: Jing and the others held the northern river bridge, linked Mount Mang to the south in formation, and joined battle with the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing held the northern river bridge and anchored his line on Mount Mang to the south, then joined the full battle.

sentences.zh: 太祖馬中流矢，驚逸，遂失所之，因此軍中擾亂。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke's horse was struck by a flying arrow, panicked and bolted, and he was lost—whereupon the army fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai's horse took a stray arrow, bolted in terror, and carried him out of sight; the army dissolved into confusion.

sentences.zh: 都督李穆下馬授太祖，軍以復振。

translations.literal: Supervisor Li Mu dismounted and gave his horse to the Grand Duke; the army thus recovered its spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Li Mu dismounted and lent Yuwen Tai his horse; the line steadied again.

sentences.zh: 於是大捷，斬高敖曹及其儀同李猛、西兗州刺史宋顯等，虜其甲士一萬五千，赴河死者以萬數。

translations.literal: Thereupon came a great victory: Gao Aocao was beheaded, along with his Army Comrade Li Meng and Western Yanzhou governor Song Xian and others; fifteen thousand armored soldiers were captured, and those who died plunging into the river numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Then came a great victory: Gao Aocao was killed, together with Army Comrade Li Meng, Western Yanzhou governor Song Xian, and others; fifteen thousand armored men were taken, and tens of thousands drowned fleeing into the river.

sentences.zh: 是日置陣旣大，首尾懸遠，從旦至未，戰數十合，氛霧四塞，莫能相知。

translations.literal: That day the battle lines were vast and head and tail far apart; from morning till we hour they fought dozens of rounds; mist filled all four quarters and neither side could know the other.
translations.idiomatic: That day the array stretched so far that van and rear could not see each other; from dawn to mid-afternoon they clashed again and again through fog so thick neither side knew where the other stood.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信、李遠居右，趙貴、怡峯居左，戰並不利，又未知魏帝及太祖所在，皆棄其卒先歸。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin and Li Yuan held the right, Zhao Gui and Yiyi Feng the left—all fought unfavorably; not knowing where the Wei emperor and the Grand Duke were, each abandoned his troops and went home first.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin and Li Yuan on the right and Zhao Gui and Yiyi Feng on the left all fared badly; unable to find the Wei emperor or Yuwen Tai, each commander abandoned his men and fled.

sentences.zh: 開府李虎、念賢等為後軍，遇信等退，即與俱還。

translations.literal: Senior Assistant Li Hu, Nian Xian, and others formed the rear guard; meeting Xin and the others retreating, they returned together with them.
translations.idiomatic: Senior Assistants Li Hu and Nian Xian commanded the rear; seeing the others retreat, they turned back with them.

sentences.zh: 由是乃班師，洛陽亦失守。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army withdrew; Luoyang too was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The army withdrew, and Luoyang fell.

sentences.zh: 大軍至弘農，守將皆已棄城西走。

translations.literal: When the main army reached Hongnong, the defending generals had all abandoned the city and fled west.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force reached Hongnong, the garrison commanders had already abandoned the city and fled west.

sentences.zh: 所虜降卒在弘農者，因相與閉門拒守。

translations.literal: The captured surrender troops at Hongnong thereupon together closed the gates and resisted in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Wei prisoners held at Hongnong then shut the gates and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 進攻拔之，誅其魁首數百人。

translations.literal: They assaulted and took it, executing several hundred ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the city, took it, and executed several hundred ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 大軍之東伐也，關中留守兵少，而前後所虜東魏士卒，皆散在民間，乃謀為亂。

translations.literal: When the main army marched east on campaign, the garrison troops left in Guanzhong were few, while Eastern Wei soldiers captured before and after were scattered among the populace; they then plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: While the main army campaigned east, Guanzhong was thinly garrisoned and captured Eastern Wei soldiers were scattered among the people; they began plotting revolt.

sentences.zh: 及李虎等至長安，計無所出，乃與公卿輔魏太子出次渭北。

translations.literal: When Li Hu and the others reached Chang'an, with no plan at hand, they together with the ministers escorted the Wei crown prince to encamp north of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hu reached Chang'an with no clear plan, he and the court ministers moved the Wei crown prince to camp north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 關中大震恐，百姓相剽劫。

translations.literal: Guanzhong was greatly alarmed; the people plundered one another.
translations.idiomatic: Panic swept Guanzhong, and people turned on one another in looting.

sentences.zh: 於是沙苑所俘軍人趙青雀、雍州民于伏德等遂反。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Shayuan-captured soldier Zhao Qingque and Yong Province commoner Yu Fude and others rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhao Qingque, a soldier taken at Shayuan, and Yu Fude of Yong Province and others rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 青雀據長安子城，伏德保咸陽，與太守慕容思慶各收降卒，以拒還師。

translations.literal: Qingque held Chang'an's inner citadel; Fude defended Xianyang; together with Administrator Murong Siqing each gathered surrender troops to resist the returning army.
translations.idiomatic: Qingque seized Chang'an's inner citadel; Fude held Xianyang; they and Xianyang governor Murong Siqing rallied surrendered troops to block the returning army.

sentences.zh: 長安大城民皆相率拒青雀，每日接戰。

translations.literal: The people of Chang'an's outer city all together resisted Qingque, fighting daily.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chang'an's outer city banded together against Qingque and fought him every day.

sentences.zh: 魏帝留止閿鄉，遣太祖討之。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor halted at Wenxiang and dispatched the Grand Duke to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor paused at Wenxiang and sent Yuwen Tai to put down the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 長安父老見太祖至，悲且喜曰：「不意今日復得見公！

translations.literal: The elders of Chang'an, seeing the Grand Duke arrive, said in grief and joy: "We never expected to see you again today!
translations.idiomatic: When the elders of Chang'an saw Yuwen Tai arrive, they wept and rejoiced: "We never thought we would see you again!

sentences.zh: 」士女咸相賀。

translations.literal: " Men and women alike congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: " Men and women alike hailed one another in celebration.

sentences.zh: 華州刺史導率軍襲咸陽，斬思慶，擒伏德，南度渭與太祖會攻青雀，破之。

translations.literal: Hua Province governor Yuwen Dao led troops in a surprise attack on Xianyang, beheaded Siqing, captured Fude, crossed the Wei southward to join the Grand Duke in attacking Qingque, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Hua governor Yuwen Dao struck Xianyang, killed Murong Siqing, captured Yu Fude, crossed the Wei southward, joined Yuwen Tai against Qingque, and broke the rebels.

sentences.zh: 太傅梁景睿先以疾留長安，遂與青雀通謀，至是亦伏誅。

translations.literal: Grand tutor Liang Jingrui, having earlier remained at Chang'an due to illness, then conspired with Qingque; at this time he too was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Liang Jingrui, who had stayed in Chang'an through illness, had secretly colluded with Qingque and was now executed as well.

sentences.zh: 關中於是乃定。

translations.literal: Guanzhong was thus settled.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong was at last pacified.

sentences.zh: 魏帝還長安，太祖復屯華州。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor returned to Chang'an; the Grand Duke again encamped at Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor returned to Chang'an, and Yuwen Tai again took post at Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，東魏將侯景攻陷廣州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, Eastern Wei general Hou Jing captured Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter Eastern Wei's Hou Jing took Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 十二月，是云寶襲洛陽，東魏將王元軌棄城走。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Shi Yunbao raided Luoyang; Eastern Wei general Wang Yuangui abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Shi Yunbao struck Luoyang; Eastern Wei's Wang Yuangui abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 都督趙剛襲廣州，拔之。

translations.literal: Supervisor Zhao Gang raided Guang Province and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor Zhao Gang retook Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 自襄、廣以西城鎮復內屬。

translations.literal: From Xiang and Guang westward, walled towns again submitted inward.
translations.idiomatic: West of Xiang and Guang, fortified towns once again returned to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，大閱於華陰。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, winter, a grand review was held at Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, winter, Yuwen Tai held a grand review at Huayin.

sentences.zh: 六年春，東魏將侯景出三鵶，將侵荊州，太祖遣開府李弼、獨孤信各率騎五千出武關，景乃退還。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, spring, Eastern Wei general Hou Jing came out through Sanya, intending to invade Jing Province; the Grand Duke sent Senior Assistants Li Bi and Dugu Xin each leading five thousand cavalry out through Wu Pass; Jing then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the sixth year Hou Jing came through Sanya Pass intending to invade Jing Province; Yuwen Tai sent Senior Assistants Li Bi and Dugu Xin, each with five thousand cavalry, out through Wu Pass, and Hou Jing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏，茹茹度河至夏州，太祖召諸軍屯沙苑以備之。

translations.literal: In summer, the Rouran crossed the river to Xia Province; the Grand Duke summoned the armies to encamp at Shayuan in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: In summer the Rouran crossed the river toward Xia Province; Yuwen Tai gathered his armies at Shayuan to meet them.

sentences.zh: 七年春三月，稽胡帥、夏州刺史劉平伏據上郡叛，遣開府于謹討平之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, spring, third month, the Jiehu chieftain and Xia Province governor Liu Pingfu held Shang commandery in rebellion; he dispatched Senior Assistant Yu Jin to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the seventh year, third month, Jiehu chieftain and Xia governor Liu Pingfu rebelled from Shang commandery; Yuwen Tai sent Senior Assistant Yu Jin to crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，太祖奏行十二條制，恐百官不勉於職事，又下令申明之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, the Grand Duke memorialized to put twelve articles of regulation into practice; fearing that the hundred officials would not exert themselves in their duties, he also issued an order clarifying them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter Yuwen Tai submitted twelve new regulations for enactment; fearing lax officials, he also issued an order spelling out their duties.

sentences.zh: 八年夏四月，大會諸軍於馬牧。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, fourth month of summer, he held a great assembly of the armies at Mabu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer of the eighth year he mustered the armies at Mabu.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，齊神武侵汾、絳，圍玉壁。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, Qi Shenwu invaded Fen and Jiang and besieged Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Qi Shenwu (Gao Huan) invaded Fen and Jiang and besieged Yubi.

sentences.zh: 太祖出軍蒲阪，將擊之。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke led troops out from Puban, intending to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai marched out from Puban to attack him.

sentences.zh: 軍至皂莢，齊神武退。

translations.literal: When the army reached Zaojia, Qi Shenwu withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Zaojia, Qi Shenwu pulled back.

sentences.zh: 太祖度汾追之，遂遁去。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke crossed the Fen in pursuit; he then fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai crossed the Fen in pursuit, and Qi Shenwu fled.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏帝狩于華陰，大饗將士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Wei emperor hunted at Huayin and held a great feast for officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Wei emperor hunted at Huayin and feasted the officers and troops.

sentences.zh: 太祖率諸將朝於行在所。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke led the generals to pay court at the imperial traveling residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai led his commanders to audience at the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 九年春，東魏北豫州刺史高仲密舉州來附，太祖帥師迎之，令開府李遠為前軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, spring, Eastern Wei Northern Yu Province governor Gao Zhongmi raised the province in submission; the Grand Duke led troops to welcome him and ordered Senior Assistant Li Yuan as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the ninth year Eastern Wei's Northern Yu governor Gao Zhongmi defected with his province; Yuwen Tai marched to receive him and put Senior Assistant Li Yuan in the van.

sentences.zh: 至洛陽，遣開府于謹攻栢谷塢，拔之。

translations.literal: Reaching Luoyang, he sent Senior Assistant Yu Jin to attack Baigu fortified camp and took it.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang he sent Senior Assistant Yu Jin to storm Baigu fortress and took it.

sentences.zh: 三月，齊神武至河北。

translations.literal: In the third month, Qi Shenwu reached the north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Qi Shenwu (Gao Huan) reached the north bank.

sentences.zh: 太祖還軍瀍上以引之。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke withdrew the army to the north bank of the Chan to lure him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai withdrew to the north bank of the Chan to draw him on.

sentences.zh: 齊神武果度河，據邙山為陣，不進者數日。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu indeed crossed the river, took Mount Mang in formation, and did not advance for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu crossed the river, formed on Mount Mang, and held his ground for days without advancing.

sentences.zh: 太祖留輜重于瀍曲，士皆銜枚，夜登邙山。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke left baggage wagons at the bend of the Chan; the soldiers all carried gag-sticks in their mouths and climbed Mount Mang by night.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai left the baggage at the bend of the Chan; the men marched in silence by night up Mount Mang.

sentences.zh: 未明，擊之，齊神武單騎為賀拔勝所逐，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Before dawn they struck; Qi Shenwu alone on horseback was pursued by Helba Sheng and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn they attacked; Qi Shenwu, alone on horseback, was chased by Helba Sheng and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 太祖率右軍若干惠等大破齊神武軍，悉虜其步卒。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke led the right wing with Ruogan Hui and others to rout Qi Shenwu's army utterly, capturing all his foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai's right wing under Ruogan Hui and others shattered Qi Shenwu's army and took every foot soldier.

sentences.zh: 趙貴等五將軍居左，戰不利。

translations.literal: Zhao Gui and five other generals held the left; the battle went unfavorably.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui and five other commanders on the left fared badly.

sentences.zh: 齊神武軍復合，太祖又不利，夜乃引還。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu's army regrouped; the Grand Duke again had the worse of it; by night he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Shenwu's forces rallied, Yuwen Tai was pressed again and withdrew by night.

sentences.zh: 旣入關，屯渭上。

translations.literal: Once inside the passes, he encamped on the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Back inside the passes, he camped on the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 齊神武進至陝，開府達奚武等率軍禦之，乃退。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu advanced to Shan; Senior Assistants Daxi Wu and others led troops to resist him, and he then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu pushed to Shan; Senior Assistants Daxi Wu and others blocked him, and he retreated.

sentences.zh: 太祖以邙山之戰，諸將失律，上表請自貶。

translations.literal: Because of the battle at Mount Mang the generals had violated discipline; the Grand Duke submitted a memorial requesting self-demotion.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle on Mount Mang, with his commanders having broken discipline, Yuwen Tai memorialized asking to demote himself.

sentences.zh: 魏帝報曰：「公膺期作宰，義高匡合，仗鉞專征，舉無遺算。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor replied: "You have assumed your term as chief minister; your righteousness in supporting the union is lofty; bearing the axe you conduct independent campaigns, and in action nothing is miscalculated.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor answered: "You took up the chief ministry at the appointed hour; your loyalty in restoring order is exalted; bearing the battle-axe you lead campaigns on your own authority, and your plans miss nothing.

sentences.zh: 朕所以垂拱九載，實資元輔之力，俾九服寧謐，誠賴翊贊之功。

translations.literal: It is for this that I have ruled at ease for nine years, truly relying on the chief minister's power, enabling the nine domains to be tranquil and peaceful—it truly depends on your assisting and supporting merit.
translations.idiomatic: For nine years I have ruled with hands folded, truly by the chief minister's strength; the nine domains are quiet and at peace, and that is your supporting work.

sentences.zh: 今大寇未殄，而以諸將失律，便欲自貶，深虧體國之誠。

translations.literal: Now the great enemy is not yet exterminated, yet because the generals violated discipline you wish to demote yourself—this deeply falls short of the sincerity owed to cherishing the state.
translations.idiomatic: The great enemy is not yet destroyed, yet because the generals broke ranks you would demote yourself—this deeply fails the loyalty the state requires of you.

sentences.zh: 宜抑此謙光，恤予一人。

translations.literal: You should suppress this modest yielding and show concern for me alone.
translations.idiomatic: Set aside this humility and think of me alone.

sentences.zh: 」於是廣募關隴豪右，以增軍旅。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he widely recruited the powerful families of Guan and Long to increase the army.
translations.idiomatic: " He then raised troops widely among the great clans of Guan and Long to strengthen the army.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，大閱于櫟陽，還屯華州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, a grand review was held at Liyang; he then returned to encamp at Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he held a grand review at Liyang, then returned to camp at Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 十年夏五月，太祖入朝。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, fifth month of summer, the Grand Duke attended court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer of the tenth year Yuwen Tai went to court.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，魏帝以太祖前後所上二十四條及十二條新制，方為中興永式，乃命尚書蘇綽更損益之，總為五卷，班於天下。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, because the twenty-four articles and twelve new regulations the Grand Duke had submitted before and after were just becoming the enduring pattern of revival, the Wei emperor ordered Minister Su Chuo to revise and adjust them further, compile them in five volumes total, and promulgate them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, taking Yuwen Tai's earlier twenty-four articles and twelve new statutes as the lasting model of restoration, the Wei emperor had Minister Su Chuo revise them into five volumes and promulgate them empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 於是搜簡賢才，以為牧守令長，皆依新制而遣焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he searched out and selected talented men to serve as prefectural governors, district governors, and magistrates, and dispatched them all according to the new regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Talented men were sought out and appointed prefects, district chiefs, and magistrates, all sent out under the new code.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，百姓便之。

translations.literal: Within several years the common people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the people felt the benefit.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，大閱於白水。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, a grand review was held at Baishui.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he held a grand review at Baishui.

sentences.zh: 十一年春三月，令曰：

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, spring, third month, an order stated:
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the eleventh year, third month, Yuwen Tai issued an order:

sentences.zh: 古之帝王所以外建諸侯內立百官者，非欲富貴其身而尊榮之，蓋以天下至廣，非一人所能獨治，是以博訪賢才，助己為治。

translations.literal: The ancient emperors and kings established feudatories without and set up the hundred offices within—not to enrich their persons and honor them with glory, but because the realm is vast beyond measure and one man cannot govern it alone; therefore they widely sought out talented men to aid them in governing.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings raised feudal lords without and appointed ministers within—not to heap wealth and honor on themselves, but because the realm is too vast for one man to rule alone; they searched widely for able men to help them govern.

sentences.zh: 若其知賢也，則以禮命之。

translations.literal: When they recognized the worthy, they appointed them with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When they found the worthy, they summoned them with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其人聞命之日，則慘然曰：「凡受人之事，任人之勞，何舍己而從人。

translations.literal: On the day such a man heard the appointment, he would mournfully say: "To accept another's commission and bear another's labor—why abandon oneself to follow others?
translations.idiomatic: On the day he received the summons, the worthy man would grieve and say: "To take another's charge and bear another's burden—why leave myself behind to serve another?

sentences.zh: 」又自勉曰：「天生儁士，所以利時。

translations.literal: " Then he would encourage himself: "Heaven born outstanding men to benefit the age.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he would steel himself: "Heaven breeds exceptional men for the sake of the age.

sentences.zh: 彼人主者，欲與我為治，安可苟辭。

translations.literal: That ruler wishes to govern with me—how can I casually decline?
translations.idiomatic: The ruler wishes to govern with my help—how can I lightly refuse?

sentences.zh: 」於是降心而受命。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he lowered his heart and accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: " And so he humbled himself and accepted the charge.

sentences.zh: 及居官也，則晝不甘食，夜不甘寢，思所以上匡人主，下安百姓；

translations.literal: Once in office, he would find no pleasure in eating by day or sleeping by night, thinking how to support the ruler above and settle the people below;
translations.idiomatic: In office he took no ease by day or rest by night, striving to support the ruler above and secure the people below;

sentences.zh: 不遑恤其私而憂其家，故妻子或有饑寒之弊而不顧也。

translations.literal: having no leisure to care for private affairs while worrying for the state, so that wife and children might suffer hunger and cold yet he would not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: with no time for private cares while the realm weighed on him, so that wife and children might know hunger and cold and he would not turn aside.

sentences.zh: 於是人主賜之以俸祿，尊之以軒冕，而不以為惠也。

translations.literal: Thereupon the ruler granted him salary and stipends, honored him with chariots and caps, yet neither regarded this as a favor.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler then paid him salary and honored him with carriage and cap, yet counted it no special grace.

sentences.zh: 賢臣受之，亦不以為德也。

translations.literal: The worthy minister in receiving it likewise did not regard it as a virtue owed him.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy minister, in accepting, likewise felt no debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 位不虛加，祿不妄賜。

translations.literal: Posts were not given without cause; stipends not bestowed rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Rank was not given in vain; salary not handed out at random.

sentences.zh: 為人君者，誠能以此道授官，為人臣者，誠能以此情受位，則天下之大，可不言而治矣。

translations.literal: If a ruler could truly confer office by this way, and a minister truly accept position with this feeling, then the vast realm could be governed without a word.
translations.idiomatic: If rulers truly appointed by this principle and ministers truly served in this spirit, the wide realm would be governed without another word spoken.

sentences.zh: 昔堯、舜之為君，稷、契之為臣，用此道也。

translations.literal: Of old, when Yao and Shun were rulers and Ji and Qi were ministers, they used this way.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Yao and Shun as rulers and Ji and Qi as ministers followed this way.

sentences.zh: 及後世衰微，此道遂廢，乃以官職為私恩，爵祿為榮惠。

translations.literal: When later ages declined, this way was abandoned; office was treated as private favor, rank and stipend as glory and bounty.
translations.idiomatic: When later ages decayed, the way was lost; office became a private favor, rank and salary a personal windfall.

sentences.zh: 人君之命官也，親則授之，愛則任之。

translations.literal: When rulers appointed officials, they gave posts to kin and entrusted offices to favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers gave posts to relatives and entrusted office to those they loved.

sentences.zh: 人臣之受位也，可以尊身而潤屋者，則迂道而求之；

translations.literal: When ministers accepted positions, if they could honor their persons and enrich their households, they would pursue them by crooked paths;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers, if rank could elevate their persons and fill their houses, would pursue it by devious means;

sentences.zh: 損身而利物者，則巧言而辭之。

translations.literal: Those who would harm themselves to benefit others, they use clever words to decline.
translations.idiomatic: Posts that demanded self-sacrifice for the public good were refused with polished excuses.

sentences.zh: 於是至公之道沒，而姦詐之萌生。

translations.literal: Thus the way of utmost fairness perished, and treachery and deceit arose.
translations.idiomatic: Impartial appointment died out, and fraud took root.

sentences.zh: 天下不治，正為此矣。

translations.literal: The realm fell to disorder—precisely for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the empire ceased to be well governed.

sentences.zh: 今聖主中興，思去澆偽。

translations.literal: Now the sage ruler restores the dynasty, intending to remove shallow falsity.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the throne is restored, the court seeks to strip away shallow pretense.

sentences.zh: 諸在朝之士，當念職事之艱難，負闕之招累，夙夜兢兢，如臨深履薄。

translations.literal: All officials at court should bear in mind the hardship of their duties and the entanglements summoned by neglect, vigilant day and night as if treading on thin ice over deep water.
translations.idiomatic: Every minister should remember how hard office is and how failure invites ruin—working day and night as if on the edge of a cliff.

sentences.zh: 才堪者，則審己而當之；

translations.literal: Those whose talent suffices should examine themselves and take the post;
translations.idiomatic: If you are fit for the role, weigh yourself honestly and accept it;

sentences.zh: 不堪者，則收短而避之。

translations.literal: Those who do not suffice should withdraw their shortcomings and avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: if not, know your limits and stand aside.

sentences.zh: 使天官不妄加，王爵不虛受，則淳素之風，庶幾可反。

translations.literal: So that celestial offices are not rashly conferred and royal ranks not received in vain, then the wind of plain sincerity might return.
translations.idiomatic: Then offices will not be handed out lightly, titles not taken empty-handed, and plain, honest government may return.

sentences.zh: 冬十月大閱於白水，遂西狩岐陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter a grand review was held at Baishui, and they then hunted west at Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yuwen Tai reviewed the troops at Baishui, then hunted west at Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，涼州刺史宇文仲和據州反。

translations.literal: In spring of the twelfth year, Liang Province governor Yuwen Zhonghe seized the province and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the twelfth year Yuwen Zhonghe, governor of Liang Province, rebelled and held the province.

sentences.zh: 瓜州民張保害刺史成慶，以州應仲和。

translations.literal: Guazhou commoner Zhang Bao killed Governor Cheng Qing and submitted the province to Zhonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bao of Guazhou murdered Governor Cheng Qing and joined Zhonghe with the province.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣開府獨孤信討之。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke sent Commissioner Dugu Xin to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai sent Dugu Xin to put them down.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣其將侯景侵襄州，太祖遣開府若干惠率輕騎擊之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent its general Hou Jing to invade Xiang Province; the Grand Duke sent Commissioner Ruogan Hui with light cavalry to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Hou Jing against Xiang Province; Yuwen Tai dispatched Ruogan Hui with light cavalry to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 至穰，景遁去。

translations.literal: Reaching Rang, Jing fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Rang, Hou Jing withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，獨孤信平涼州，擒仲和，遷其民六千餘家于長安。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer Dugu Xin pacified Liang Province, captured Zhonghe, and moved more than six thousand households to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Dugu Xin recovered Liang Province, took Zhonghe prisoner, and resettled over six thousand families in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 瓜州都督令狐延起義誅張保，瓜州平。

translations.literal: Guazhou inspector general Linghu Yan raised righteous arms and killed Zhang Bao; Guazhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Yan, inspector of Guazhou, rose in loyal revolt and killed Zhang Bao; Guazhou was secured.

sentences.zh: 七月，太祖大會諸軍於咸陽。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the Grand Duke held a great assembly of all armies at Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yuwen Tai mustered the armies at Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，齊神武圍玉壁，大都督韋孝寬力戰拒守，齊神武攻圍六旬不能下，其士卒死者什二三。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Qi Shenwu besieged Yubi; Grand Commander Wei Xiaokuan fought fiercely to hold; Qi Shenwu assaulted and besieged for sixty days without taking it; of his soldiers two or three in ten died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Qi Shenwu besieged Yubi; Wei Xiaokuan held out in fierce fighting. After sixty days of assault Qi Shenwu still could not take the city, and two or three tenths of his troops were dead.

sentences.zh: 會齊神武有疾，燒營而退。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu fell ill, he burned camp and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Shenwu then fell ill, burned his camp, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 三月，太祖遣開府李弼率軍援之，軌等遁去。

translations.literal: In the third month the Grand Duke sent Commissioner Li Bi with an army to aid them; Gui and the others fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Yuwen Tai sent Li Bi with reinforcements; Gui and his colleagues withdrew.

sentences.zh: 景請留收輯河南，遂徙鎮豫州。

translations.literal: Jing asked permission to stay and gather order in Henan, and moved to garrison Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing asked to remain and restore order in Henan, and shifted his garrison to Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是遣開府王思政據潁川，弼引軍還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Commissioner Wang Sizheng to hold Yingchuan, and Bi led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai then posted Wang Sizheng at Yingchuan while Li Bi brought the main force home.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，侯景密圖附梁。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Hou Jing secretly planned to attach himself to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Hou Jing began secretly plotting to go over to Liang.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其謀，悉追還前後所配景將士。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke learned of the plot and recalled all officers and soldiers previously assigned to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai discovered the scheme and recalled every officer and soldier he had lent Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 景懼，遂叛。

translations.literal: Jing was afraid and thereupon rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing, alarmed, rebelled.

sentences.zh: 冬，太祖奉魏帝西狩於岐陽。

translations.literal: In winter the Grand Duke accompanied the Wei emperor on a western hunt at Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Yuwen Tai escorted the Wei emperor on a western hunt at Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 十四年春，魏帝詔封太祖長子毓為寧都郡公，食邑三千戶。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourteenth year the Wei emperor decreed enfeoffment of the Grand Duke's eldest son Yu as Duke of Ningdu commandery, with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fourteenth year the Wei emperor enfeoffed Yuwen Tai's eldest son Yuwen Yu as duke of Ningdu commandery with three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖以平元顥、納孝莊帝之功，封寧都縣子，至是改縣為郡，而以封毓，用彰勤王之始也。

translations.literal: Earlier the Grand Duke had been enfeoffed as viscount of Ningdu county for pacifying Yuan Hao and receiving Emperor Xiaozhuang; now the county was changed to a commandery and Yu was enfeoffed with it, to manifest the beginning of his loyal service to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai had first received Ningdu as a county viscount for defeating Yuan Hao and restoring Emperor Xiaozhuang; now the county was raised to a commandery and given to Yuwen Yu, marking the origin of the family's service to the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，進授太祖太師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer the Grand Duke was further invested as grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yuwen Tai was promoted to grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 太祖奉魏太子巡撫西境，自新平出安定，登隴，刻石紀事。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke accompanied the Wei crown prince on a tour of the western frontier, left from Xinping toward Anding, ascended Long, and carved stone to record the event.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai escorted the Wei crown prince on a tour of the western frontier, marching from Xinping through Anding, crossing Long, and carving an inscription on stone.

sentences.zh: 下安陽，至原州，曆北長城，大狩。

translations.literal: He descended to Anyang, reached Yuan Province, traveled along the northern Long Wall, and held a grand hunt.
translations.idiomatic: He went down to Anyang, reached Yuan Province, followed the northern Long Wall, and held a great hunt.

sentences.zh: 將東趣五原，至蒲川，聞魏帝不豫，遂還。

translations.literal: About to turn east toward Wuyuan, when they reached Puchuan they heard the Wei emperor was indisposed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: As he was turning east toward Wuyuan, word at Puchuan that the Wei emperor was ill brought him back.

sentences.zh: 旣至，帝疾已愈，於是還華州。

translations.literal: When they arrived the emperor's illness had already healed, and they then returned to Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he arrived the emperor had recovered, and he returned to Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 是歲，東魏遣其將高岳、慕容紹宗、劉豐生等，率衆十餘萬圍王思政於潁川。

translations.literal: That year Eastern Wei sent its generals Gao Yue, Murong Shaozong, Liu Fengsheng, and others, leading more than a hundred thousand men to besiege Wang Sizheng at Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Eastern Wei sent Gao Yue, Murong Shaozong, Liu Fengsheng, and others with over a hundred thousand men to besiege Wang Sizheng at Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，太祖遣大將軍趙貴帥軍至穰，兼督東南諸州兵以援思政。

translations.literal: In spring of the fifteenth year the Grand Duke sent Grand General Zhao Gui at the head of an army to Rang, concurrently supervising the armies of the southeastern provinces to aid Sizheng.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fifteenth year Yuwen Tai sent Zhao Gui to Rang to command the southeastern provinces' forces in relief of Wang Sizheng.

sentences.zh: 高岳起堰，引洧水以灌城，自潁川以北皆為陂澤，救兵不得至。

translations.literal: Gao Yue raised a dam, diverted the Wei River to flood the city; from north of Yingchuan all became marshes, and relief troops could not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yue built a dam and diverted the Wei River into the city; north of Yingchuan the land turned to swamp and relief could not get through.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，潁川陷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer Yingchuan fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yingchuan fell.

sentences.zh: 初，侯景自豫州附梁，後遂度江，圍建業。

translations.literal: Earlier Hou Jing from Yuzhou had attached himself to Liang; afterward he crossed the Yangtze and besieged Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing had earlier defected from Yuzhou to Liang, then crossed the Yangtze and besieged Jianye.

sentences.zh: 梁司州刺史柳仲禮以本朝有難，帥兵援之。

translations.literal: Liang's governor of Si Province Liu Zhongli, because the court was in peril, led troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhongli, Liang governor of Si Province, marched to Hou Jing's aid when the dynasty was in crisis.

sentences.zh: 梁竟陵郡守孫暠舉郡來附，太祖使大都督符貴往鎮之。

translations.literal: Liang's Jingling commandery administrator Sun Gao submitted the whole commandery; the Grand Duke sent Grand Commander Fu Gui to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gao, administrator of Jingling in Liang territory, submitted his commandery; Yuwen Tai sent Fu Gui to hold it.

sentences.zh: 及景克建業，仲禮還司州，率衆來寇，暠以郡叛。

translations.literal: When Jing took Jianye, Zhongli returned to Si Province and led forces to raid; Gao rebelled with the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Hou Jing took Jianye, Liu Zhongli returned to Si Province and invaded; Sun Gao rebelled with Jingling.

sentences.zh: 太祖大怒。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai was furious.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，遣開府楊忠率兵與行臺僕射長孫儉討之，攻克隨郡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter he sent Commissioner Yang Zhong with troops and Chief Administrator Changsun Jian to suppress them, and captured Suicheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent Yang Zhong and Chief Administrator Changsun Jian against them and took Suicheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 忠進圍仲禮長史馬岫於安陸。

translations.literal: Zhong pressed on to besiege Zhongli's chief clerk Ma Xiu at Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong then besieged Liu Zhongli's chief clerk Ma Xiu at Anlu.

sentences.zh: 是歲，盜殺齊文襄於鄴，其弟洋討賊，擒之，仍嗣其事，是為文宣帝。

translations.literal: That year an assassin killed Qi Wenchang at Ye; his brother Yang pursued the criminal, captured him, and succeeded to his position—this was Emperor Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year an assassin killed Qi Wenchang (Gao Cheng) at Ye; his brother Gao Yang hunted down the killer, took over his power, and became Emperor Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 十六年春正月，柳仲禮率衆來援安陸，楊忠逆擊於漴頭，大破之，擒仲禮，悉虜其衆。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the sixteenth year Liu Zhongli led forces to relieve Anlu; Yang Zhong met and attacked them at Chongtou, routed them utterly, captured Zhongli, and took all his men prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixteenth year Liu Zhongli marched to relieve Anlu; Yang Zhong met him at Chongtou, crushed his army, captured him, and took his entire force.

sentences.zh: 馬岫以城降。

translations.literal: Ma Xiu surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiu surrendered Anlu.

sentences.zh: 三月，魏帝封太祖第二子震為武邑公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the third month the Wei emperor enfeoffed the Grand Duke's second son Zhen as Duke of Wuyi, fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Wei emperor enfeoffed Yuwen Tai's second son Yuwen Zhen as duke of Wuyi with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 先是，梁雍州刺史、岳陽王詧與其叔父荊州刺史、湘東王繹不睦，乃稱蕃來附，遣其世子嶚為質。

translations.literal: Earlier Liang's Yongzhou governor, Prince of Yueyang Xiao Cha, was on bad terms with his uncle, Jingzhou governor Prince of Xiangdong Xiao Yi; he declared himself a vassal and submitted, sending his heir Xiao Yan as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiao Cha, Liang prince of Yueyang and governor of Yongzhou, had quarreled with his uncle Xiao Yi, prince of Xiangdong and governor of Jingzhou; he submitted as a vassal and sent his heir Xiao Yan as hostage.

sentences.zh: 及楊忠擒仲禮，繹懼，復遣其子方平來朝。

translations.literal: When Yang Zhong captured Zhongli, Yi was afraid and again sent his son Fangping to court.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Zhong captured Liu Zhongli, Xiao Yi, alarmed, sent his son Fangping to court again.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，齊文宣廢其主元善見而自立。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer Qi Wenxuan deposed his ruler Yuan Shan Jian and declared himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Qi Wenxuan deposed Emperor Xiaojing (Yuan Shan Jian) and took the throne himself.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，太祖率諸軍東伐，拜章武公導為大將軍，總督留守諸軍事，屯涇北以鎮關中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the Grand Duke led all armies east on campaign, appointed Duke of Zhangwu Dao grand general to oversee all garrison affairs, and stationed north of the Jing to hold Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yuwen Tai marched east, made Yuwen Dao, duke of Zhangwu, grand general in charge of the home garrison, and posted him north of the Jing to guard Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 九月丁巳，軍出長安。

translations.literal: On day dingsi of the ninth month the army marched out from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day in the ninth month the army left Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時連雨，自秋及冬，諸軍馬驢多死。

translations.literal: Rains continued unceasingly; from autumn through winter many horses and mules of the armies died.
translations.idiomatic: Steady rain from autumn into winter killed large numbers of army horses and mules.

sentences.zh: 遂于弘農北造橋濟河，自蒲阪還。

translations.literal: They then built a bridge north of Hongnong to cross the river and returned by way of Puban.
translations.idiomatic: They bridged the river north of Hongnong and withdrew through Puban.

sentences.zh: 於是河南自洛陽，河北自平陽以東，遂入於齊矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Henan from Luoyang and Hebei from Pingyang eastward passed into Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Henan west of Luoyang and Hebei east of Pingyang were thus lost to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 十七年春三月，魏文帝崩，皇太子嗣位，太祖以冢宰總百揆。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring of the seventeenth year Emperor Wen of Wei died; the crown prince succeeded; the Grand Duke as minister of state directed all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventeenth year Emperor Wen died; the crown prince succeeded, and Yuwen Tai as minister of state ran the government.

sentences.zh: 梁邵陵王蕭綸侵安陸，大將軍楊忠討擒之。

translations.literal: Liang's Prince of Shaoling Xiao Lun invaded Anlu; Grand General Yang Zhong suppressed and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Lun, Liang prince of Shaoling, attacked Anlu; Yang Zhong defeated and captured him.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，太祖遣大將軍王雄出子午，伐上津、魏興；

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter the Grand Duke sent Grand General Wang Xiong out via Ziwu to attack Shangjin and Weixing;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yuwen Tai sent Wang Xiong through Ziwu Pass against Shangjin and Weixing;

sentences.zh: 大將軍達奚武出散關，伐南鄭。

translations.literal: Grand General Daxi Wu out via Sanguan to attack Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: and Daxi Wu through Sanguan against Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年春，王雄平上津、魏興，以其地置東梁州。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of the deposed Wei emperor Wang Xiong pacified Shangjin and Weixing and established Eastern Liang Province there.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of the Deposed Emperor, Wang Xiong took Shangjin and Weixing and created Eastern Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，達奚武圍南鄭，月餘，梁州刺史、宜豐侯蕭循以州降。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer Daxi Wu besieged Nanzheng for more than a month; Liang's Liangzhou governor Marquis of Yifeng Xiao Xun surrendered the province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Daxi Wu besieged Nanzheng for over a month until Xiao Xun, Liang governor of Liangzhou and marquis of Yifeng, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 武執循還長安。

translations.literal: Wu seized Xun and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Wu took Xiao Xun back to Chang'an as prisoner.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，東梁州民叛，率衆圍州城，太祖復遣王雄討之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn Eastern Liang Province people rebelled, led a host to besiege the provincial city; the Grand Duke again sent Wang Xiong to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Eastern Liang Province rose in revolt and besieged the capital; Yuwen Tai sent Wang Xiong again to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 侯景之克建業也，還奉梁武帝為主。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing took Jianye he still acknowledged Liang Wudi as sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing captured Jianye he still recognized Liang Wudi as emperor.

sentences.zh: 居數旬，梁武以憤恚薨。

translations.literal: After several tens of days Liang Wudi died of wrath and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Within weeks Liang Wudi died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 景又立其子綱，尋而廢綱自立。

translations.literal: Jing then installed his son Gang, but soon deposed Gang and declared himself ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing then enthroned Liang Wudi's son Gang, but soon deposed him and seized power himself.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，綱弟繹討景，擒之，遣其舍人魏彥來告，仍嗣位於江陵，是為元帝。

translations.literal: After more than a year Gang's brother Yi campaigned against Jing, captured him, sent his retainer Wei Yan to report, and succeeded to the throne at Jiangling—this was Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Gang's brother Xiao Yi destroyed Hou Jing, sent his retainer Wei Yan with the news, and took the throne at Jiangling as Emperor Yuan (Yuan Di).

sentences.zh: 二年春，魏帝詔太祖去丞相大行臺，為都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year the Wei emperor decreed that the Grand Duke leave the posts of chancellor and commissioner-in-chief and become supervisor of all armies at home and abroad.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year the Wei emperor stripped Yuwen Tai of the chancellorship and grand commissionerate, leaving him supervisor of all armies at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 二月，東梁州平，遷其豪帥於雍州。

translations.literal: In the second month Eastern Liang Province was pacified; its powerful clan heads were moved to Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Eastern Liang Province was pacified and its leading families were resettled in Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 三月，太祖遣大將軍、魏安公尉遲迥率衆伐梁武陵王蕭紀於蜀。

translations.literal: In the third month the Grand Duke sent Grand General Duke of Wei'an Yuchi Jiong with troops to campaign against Liang's Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Yuwen Tai sent Yuchi Jiong, duke of Wei'an, against Xiao Ji, Liang prince of Wuling, in Shu.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，太祖勒銳騎三萬西踰隴，度金城河，至姑臧。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer the Grand Duke mustered thirty thousand crack cavalry, crossed Long westward, forded the Jincheng River, and reached Guzang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Yuwen Tai led thirty thousand elite cavalry west over Long, crossed the Jincheng River, and reached Guzang.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾震懼，遣使獻其方物。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun was shaken with fear and sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun, terrified, sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 五月，蕭紀潼州刺史楊乾運以州降，引迥軍向成都。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Xiao Ji's Tong Province governor Yang Qianyun surrendered the province and led Jiong's army toward Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yang Qianyun, Xiao Ji's governor of Tong Province, surrendered and guided Yuchi Jiong toward Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，太祖自姑臧至於長安。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the Grand Duke went from Guzang to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yuwen Tai returned from Guzang to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 八月，克成都，劍南平。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Chengdu was taken and Jiannan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Chengdu fell and Jiannan was pacified.
