sentences.zh: 冬十一月，尚書元烈謀作亂，事發，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter Minister of Works Yuan Lie plotted rebellion; when the affair broke out he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Minister Yuan Lie plotted revolt; exposed, he was executed.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月，始作九命之典，以敘內外官爵。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the third year they first enacted the Nine Ranks code to order civil and military office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year the Nine Ranks system was introduced to rank civil and military offices.

sentences.zh: 以第一品為九命，第九品為一命。

translations.literal: The first grade was nine ranks, the ninth grade one rank.
translations.idiomatic: First grade became nine ranks; ninth grade, one rank.

sentences.zh: 改流外品為九秩，亦以九為上。

translations.literal: The grades outside the regular stream were changed to nine orders, also taking nine as highest.
translations.idiomatic: Extra-statutory grades were reorganized into nine orders, with nine again the highest.

sentences.zh: 又改置州郡及縣：改東雍為華州，北雍為宜州，南雍為蔡州，華州為同州，北華為鄜州，東秦為隴州，南秦為成州，北秦為交州，東荊為淮州，南荊為昌州，東夏為延州，南夏為長州，東梁為金州，南梁為隆州，北梁為靜州，陽都為汾州，南汾為勳州，汾州為丹州，南豳為寧州，南岐為鳳州，南洛為上州，南廣為淯州，南襄為湖州，西涼為甘州，西郢為鴻州，西益為利州，東巴為集州，北應為輔州，恆州為均州，沙州為深州，寧州為麓州，義州為岩州，新州為溫州，江州為沔州，西安為鹽州，安州為始州，幷州為隨州，肆州為塘州，冀州為順州，淮州為純州，揚州為潁州，司州為憲州，南平為昇州，南郢為歸州，青州為眉州。

translations.literal: They also altered the establishment of provinces, commanderies, and counties: Eastern Yong was changed to Hua Province, Northern Yong to Yi Province, Southern Yong to Cai Province, Hua to Tong Province, Northern Hua to Fu Province, Eastern Qin to Long Province, Southern Qin to Cheng Province, Northern Qin to Jiao Province, Eastern Jing to Huai Province, Southern Jing to Chang Province, Eastern Xia to Yan Province, Southern Xia to Long Province, Eastern Liang to Jin Province, Southern Liang to Long Province, Northern Liang to Jing Province, Yangdu to Fen Province, Southern Fen to Xun Province, Fen to Dan Province, Southern Bin to Ning Province, Southern Qi to Feng Province, Southern Luo to Shang Province, Southern Guang to Yu Province, Southern Xiang to Hu Province, Western Liang to Gan Province, Western Ying to Hong Province, Western Yi to Li Province, Eastern Ba to Ji Province, Northern Ying to Fu Province, Heng to Jun Province, Sha to Shen Province, Ning to Lu Province, Yi to Yan Province, Xin to Wen Province, Jiang to Mian Province, Xi'an to Yan Province, An to Shi Province, Bing to Sui Province, Si to Tang Province, Ji to Shun Province, Huai to Chun Province, Yang to Ying Province, Si to Xian Province, Southern Ping to Sheng Province, Southern Ying to Gui Province, Qing to Mei Province.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces, commanderies, and counties were also reorganized: Eastern Yong became Hua; Northern Yong, Yi; Southern Yong, Cai; Hua, Tong; Northern Hua, Fu; Eastern Qin, Long; Southern Qin, Cheng; Northern Qin, Jiao; Eastern Jing, Huai; Southern Jing, Chang; Eastern Xia, Yan; Southern Xia, Long; Eastern Liang, Jin; Southern Liang, Long; Northern Liang, Jing; Yangdu, Fen; Southern Fen, Xun; Fen, Dan; Southern Bin, Ning; Southern Qi, Feng; Southern Luo, Shang; Southern Guang, Yu; Southern Xiang, Hu; Western Liang, Gan; Western Ying, Hong; Western Yi, Li; Eastern Ba, Ji; Northern Ying, Fu; Heng, Jun; Sha, Shen; Ning, Lu; Yi, Yan; Xin, Wen; Jiang, Mian; Xi'an, Yan; An, Shi; Bing, Sui; Si (肆), Tang; Ji, Shun; Huai, Chun; Yang, Ying; Si (司), Xian; Southern Ping, Sheng; Southern Ying, Gui; Qing, Mei.

sentences.zh: 凡改州四十六，置州一，改郡一百六，改縣二百三十。

translations.literal: In all forty-six provinces were renamed, one province established, one hundred six commanderies renamed, and two hundred thirty counties renamed.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-six provinces were renamed, one created, and one hundred six commanderies and two hundred thirty counties retitled.

sentences.zh: 自元烈誅，魏帝有怨言。

translations.literal: Since Yuan Lie was executed the Wei emperor had resentful words.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Lie's execution the Wei emperor voiced bitter complaints.

sentences.zh: 魏淮安王育、廣平王贊等垂泣諫之，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Wei Prince of Huai'an Yu, Prince of Guangping Zan, and others wept as they remonstrated; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Yu of Huai'an and Zan of Guangping pleaded with tears; the emperor refused to heed them.

sentences.zh: 於是太祖與公卿定議，廢帝，尊立齊王廓，是為恭帝。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Grand Duke with the grandees resolved to depose the emperor and install Prince of Qi Kuo as sovereign—this was Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai then joined the senior officials in deposing him and enthroning Yuan Kuo, prince of Qi, as Emperor Gong (Gong Di).

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年夏四月，帝大饗羣臣。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer of the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei the emperor held a great feast for the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Emperor Gong's first year the court held a grand banquet for the ministers.

sentences.zh: 魏史柳虯執簡書於朝曰：「廢帝，文皇帝之嗣子。

translations.literal: Wei Historiographer Liu Biao held the bamboo records at court and said: "The deposed emperor was the heir son of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At court Wei historiographer Liu Biao read from the annals: "The deposed emperor was Emperor Wen's heir.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，文皇帝托于安定公曰：『是子才，由於公，不才，亦由於公，宜勉之。

translations.literal: At age seven Emperor Wen entrusted him to the Duke of Anding, saying: 'Whether this child has talent is due to you; if he lacks talent, that too is due to you—you should exert yourself.'
translations.idiomatic: At seven Emperor Wen entrusted him to the duke of Anding with the words: 'Whether this boy proves capable rests with you; if he fails, that too is yours—see that you teach him well.'

sentences.zh: 』公旣受茲重寄，居元輔之任，又納女為皇后，遂不能訓誨有成，致令廢黜，負文皇帝付屬之意，此咎非安定公而誰？

translations.literal: The Duke received this weighty trust, held the position of chief minister, and also gave his daughter as empress—yet could not instruct him to completion, leading to deposition; failing Emperor Wen's entrustment—who bears this blame if not the Duke of Anding?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai accepted that charge as chief minister, gave his daughter as empress, yet failed to train him and brought about his removal—who but the duke of Anding betrayed Emperor Wen's trust?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖乃令太常盧辯作誥諭公卿曰：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: The Grand Duke then ordered the Minister of Rites Lu Bian to compose an announcement to the grandees, saying: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai had Minister of Rites Lu Bian draft a proclamation to the officials: "Alas!

sentences.zh: 我羣后暨衆士，維文皇帝以繈褓之嗣托於予，訓之誨之，庶厥有成。

translations.literal: My lords and all officers—the late Emperor Wen entrusted to me an heir in swaddling clothes; I instructed and admonished him, hoping he might come to fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: My lords and officers—Emperor Wen left me an infant heir; I was to teach and guide him to maturity.

sentences.zh: 而予罔能革變厥心，庸暨乎廢，墜我文皇帝之志。

translations.literal: Yet I could not alter his heart, and he came to deposition, failing the late Emperor Wen's aim.
translations.idiomatic: I could not change his heart, and he was deposed—Emperor Wen's hope is undone.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 茲咎予其焉避。

translations.literal: For this fault where can I escape?
translations.idiomatic: For this fault I cannot escape blame.

sentences.zh: 予實知之，矧爾衆人之心哉。

translations.literal: I know it truly—how much more do all of you know it in your hearts.
translations.idiomatic: I know it full well—and so do you, in your hearts.

sentences.zh: 惟予之顏，豈惟今厚，將恐來世以予為口實。

translations.literal: As for my face—it is not shameful only today; I fear posterity will take me as a byword.
translations.idiomatic: My disgrace is not for this day alone; posterity will make me a proverb of failure.

sentences.zh: 」乙亥，詔封太祖子邕為輔城公，憲為安城公，邑各二千戶。

translations.literal: On day yihai a decree enfeoffed the Grand Duke's sons Yong as Duke of Fucheng and Xian as Duke of Ancheng, fief of two thousand households each.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day the emperor enfeoffed Yuwen Tai's sons Yuwen Yong as duke of Fucheng and Yuwen Xian as duke of Ancheng, two thousand households each.

sentences.zh: 茹茹乙旃達官寇廣武。

translations.literal: Rouran Yizhan Daguan raided Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Rouran chieftain Yizhan Daguan raided Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 五月，遣柱國趙貴追擊之，斬首數千級，收其輜重而還。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he sent Pillar of State Zhao Gui in pursuit, beheaded several thousand, seized their baggage train, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhao Gui pursued them, killed several thousand, captured their baggage, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，太祖西狩至於原州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the Grand Duke hunted west as far as Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Yuwen Tai hunted west to Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝遣使請據舊圖以定疆界，又連結於齊，言辭悖慢。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang sent envoys requesting to fix the borders according to the old maps, and also allied with Qi; his words were perverse and insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang sent envoys asking that borders be drawn from old maps, allied himself with Northern Qi, and spoke with brazen insolence.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「古人有言『天之所棄，誰能興之』，其蕭繹之謂乎。」

translations.literal: The Grand Duke said: "The ancients had a saying, 'Whom Heaven abandons, who can raise up?'—is this not meant of Xiao Yi?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai said: "The ancients said, 'Whom Heaven rejects, who can restore?'—surely that applies to Xiao Yi."

sentences.zh: 冬十月壬戌，遣柱國于謹、中山公護、大將軍楊忠、韋孝寬等步騎五萬討之。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, day renxu, he dispatched the pillar-of-state Yu Jin, the Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Hu, Grand General Yang Zhong, Wei Xiaokuan, and others with fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on renxu day, he sent Pillar-of-State Yu Jin, Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Hu, Grand General Yang Zhong, Wei Xiaokuan, and others with fifty thousand foot and horse to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 十一月癸未，師濟於漢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, day guimwei, the army crossed the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on guimwei day, the army crossed the Han.

sentences.zh: 中山公護與楊忠率銳騎先屯其城下，據江津以備其逸。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Hu and Yang Zhong led crack cavalry to encamp first below the city, holding the Yangtze ferry to guard against escape.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu and Yang Zhong led elite cavalry to the foot of the walls first and held the river crossing to block any breakout.

sentences.zh: 丙申，謹至江陵，列營圍守。

translations.literal: On bingshen day Jin reached Jiangling and arrayed camps to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Yu Jin reached Jiangling and laid siege.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，進攻城，其日克之。

translations.literal: On xinhai day they pressed the attack on the city, and that same day took it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day they stormed the city and took it that same day.

sentences.zh: 擒梁元帝，殺之，幷虜其百官及士民以歸。

translations.literal: They captured Emperor Yuan of Liang, killed him, and together made captives of his hundred officials and gentry and people, taking them back.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Emperor Yuan, executed him, and marched off his officials, gentry, and common people as captives.

sentences.zh: 沒為奴婢者十餘萬，其免者二百餘家。

translations.literal: Those made slave girls and servants numbered more than a hundred thousand; those spared amounted to a little over two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand were enslaved; only some two hundred households were spared.

sentences.zh: 立蕭詧為梁主，居江陵，為魏附庸。

translations.literal: They installed Xiao Cha as Liang ruler, dwelling at Jiangling, as Wei's vassal.
translations.idiomatic: They enthroned Xiao Cha as Liang king at Jiangling, a Wei client.

sentences.zh: 梁將王僧辯、陳霸先于丹陽立梁元帝第九子方智為主。

translations.literal: The Liang generals Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian at Danyang established Emperor Yuan's ninth son Fangzhi as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: At Danyang, Liang generals Wang Sengbian and Chen Baxian raised Yuan's ninth son Fangzhi as emperor.

sentences.zh: 魏氏之初，統國三十六，大姓九十九，後多絕滅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wei rule the state had thirty-six domains and ninety-nine great clans; later many died out.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei first ruled, it had thirty-six domains and ninety-nine great clans, but many had since disappeared.

sentences.zh: 至是，以諸將功高者為三十六國後，次功者為九十九姓後，所統軍人，亦改從其姓。

translations.literal: At this time those of the highest merit among the generals were made heirs of the thirty-six states, and those of the next merit heirs of the ninety-nine surnames; the soldiers they commanded were also made to change and follow their surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Generals of highest merit were now made heirs of the thirty-six states, those of lesser merit heirs of the ninety-nine clans, and the troops under them took their leaders' surnames.

sentences.zh: 二年，梁廣州刺史王琳寇邊。

translations.literal: In the second year, Wang Lin, prefect of Guangzhou in Liang, raided the borders.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Wang Lin, Liang prefect of Guangzhou, attacked the frontier.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月，遣大將軍豆盧寧帥師討之。

translations.literal: In winter, eleventh month, he dispatched Grand General Dou Lu Ning to lead the army to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter he sent Grand General Dou Lu Ning against him.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月丁丑，初行《周禮》，建六官。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, first month, day dingchou, the 《Rites of Zhou》 were first put into practice and the six offices were established.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the third year, on dingchou day of the first month, the 《Zhou Rites》 were enacted and the six ministries established.

sentences.zh: 以太祖為太師、大冢宰，柱國李弼為太傅，大司徒趙貴為太保，大宗伯獨孤信為大司馬，于謹為大司寇，侯莫陳崇為大司空。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke was made Grand Preceptor and Grand Minister; the pillar-of-state Li Bi was made Grand Tutor; Grand Minister of Education Zhao Gui was made Grand Guardian; Grand Minister of Rites Dugu Xin was made Grand Marshal; Yu Jin was made Grand Minister of Justice; Houmochen Chong was made Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai became grand preceptor and grand minister; Li Bi grand tutor; Zhao Gui grand guardian; Dugu Xin grand marshal; Yu Jin grand minister of justice; and Houmochen Chong grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖以漢魏官繁，思革前弊。

translations.literal: Earlier the Grand Duke, because Han and Wei offices were excessive, had wished to reform past abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai had long wanted to cut the bloated Han and Wei bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 大統中，乃命蘇綽、盧辯依周制改創其事，尋亦置六卿官，然為撰次未成，衆務猶歸臺閣。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he ordered Su Chuo and Lu Bian to consult the Zhou system and create and reform these matters; soon they also set up the six ministers' offices, but because the compilation was not finished, all affairs still returned to the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Datong he had Su Chuo and Lu Bian draft reforms on the Zhou model and begin setting up the six ministries, but with the work unfinished routine business still flowed through the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至是始畢，乃命行之。

translations.literal: At this time it was at last complete, and he thereupon ordered it put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: Now the scheme was complete, and he ordered it enforced.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，太祖北巡狩。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, the Grand Duke toured north on hunt.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer Yuwen Tai hunted north.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，度北河。

translations.literal: In autumn, seventh month, he crossed the northern river.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he crossed the northern river.

sentences.zh: 王琳遣使來附，以琳為大將軍、長沙郡公。

translations.literal: Wang Lin sent envoys to come and attach himself; Lin was made Grand General and Duke of Changsha commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin sent envoys to submit; he was made grand general and duke of Changsha commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏帝封太祖子直為秦郡公，招為正平公，邑各一千戶。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor enfeoffed the Grand Duke's son Zhi as Duke of Qin commandery and Zhao as Duke of Zhengping, each with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor enfeoffed Yuwen Tai's sons Zhi as duke of Qin commandery and Zhao as duke of Zhengping, each with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 九月，太祖有疾，還至雲陽，命中山公護受遺輔嗣子。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Grand Duke fell ill; returning to Yunyang he ordered the Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Hu to receive his testament and assist the heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Yuwen Tai fell ill; back at Yunyang he named Duke of Zhongshan Yuwen Hu regent to assist his heir.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙亥，崩於雲陽宮，還長安發喪。

translations.literal: In winter, tenth month, day yihai, he died at Yunyang Palace; the body was returned to Chang'an and mourning was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on yihai day, he died at Yunyang Palace; his body was brought to Chang'an and mourning began.

sentences.zh: 時年五十二。

translations.literal: At the time he was fifty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 甲申，葬於成陵，諡曰文公。

translations.literal: On day jiashen he was buried at Chengling; his posthumous title was Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day he was buried at Chengling with the posthumous name Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝受禪，追尊為文王，廟曰太祖。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin received the abdication he was posthumously honored as King Wen, and his temple title was Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne Yuwen Tai was posthumously honored as King Wen with temple name Taizu.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，追尊為文皇帝。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wucheng he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 太祖知人善任使，從諫如流，崇尚儒術，明達政事，恩信被物，能駕馭英豪，一見之者，咸思用命。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke knew men and employed them well, followed remonstrance as flowing water, honored Confucian learning, was clear in government affairs, his kindness and trust covered things, could drive and manage heroes—those who saw him once all wished to give their lives in his service.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai knew talent and put it to use, took counsel readily, honored the classics, governed with clarity, and won hearts with grace and good faith; heroes who met him once wanted to die for him.

sentences.zh: 沙苑所獲囚俘，釋而用之，河橋之役，率以擊戰，皆得其死力。

translations.literal: Prisoners taken at Shachu he released and employed them; at the battle of the river bridge he always led them to strike in battle, and all exerted their utmost strength unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Captives from Shayuan he freed and enlisted; at the River Bridge battle he sent them into the line, and they fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 諸將出征，授以方略，無不制勝。

translations.literal: When generals went on campaign he entrusted them with strategy, and none failed to win.
translations.idiomatic: When his generals marched out he gave them the plan, and they never lost.

sentences.zh: 性好朴素，不尚虛飾，恆以反風俗，復古始為心。

translations.literal: By nature he loved plain simplicity and did not esteem empty ornament; he always took as his heart to reverse corrupt custom and restore antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and spare by nature, he scorned show and aimed always to turn custom back toward the ancients.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：水曆將終，羣凶放命，或威權震主，或釁逆滔天。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The water calendar was about to end; the wicked gave free rein to their lives—some whose authority and power shook their lords, some whose sedition and treason flooded heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: As the Northern Wei dynasty reached its end, villains ran rampant—some so powerful they overshadowed their emperors, others so treasonous their crimes seemed to touch the sky.

sentences.zh: 咸謂大寶可以力征，神物可以求得，莫不闚窬九鼎，睥睨兩宮，而誅夷繼及，亡不旋踵。

translations.literal: All thought the great treasure could be taken by force of arms and the divine vessel could be sought and obtained; none failed to peep at the Nine Cauldrons and look down on the two palaces—and executions and exterminations followed in succession, perishing without turning the heel.
translations.idiomatic: Each believed the throne could be seized by the sword and the mandate wrested by force; all coveted the imperial regalia and eyed the palace—yet one after another they were destroyed, dying almost before they could turn around.

sentences.zh: 是知巨君篡盜，終成建武之資；

translations.literal: Thus one knows that the great usurper Wang Mang's theft at last became capital for the Jianwu restoration;
translations.idiomatic: So it proved that Wang Mang's usurpation only furnished the means for Guangwu's restoration;

sentences.zh: 仲潁兇殘，實啟當塗之業。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo's brutality in truth opened the career of the house of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: and Dong Zhuo's savagery truly opened the way for Cao Wei.

sentences.zh: 天命有底，庸可滔乎。

translations.literal: Heaven's mandate has its foundation—how could it be flooded over.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate rests on something firmer than force—who could overwhelm it.

sentences.zh: 太祖田無一成，衆無一旅，驅馳戎馬之際，躡足行伍之間。

translations.literal: The Grand Duke had not one field in his name, not one brigade in his host; he drove amid the rush of war-steeds and stepped in the ranks of marching soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai began with not a field to his name nor a company to his command, riding hard through war and trudging in the ranks with common soldiers.

sentences.zh: 屬與能之時，應啟聖之運，鳩集義勇，糾合同盟，一舉而殄仇讐，再駕而匡帝室。

translations.literal: When the age brought forth the able, he answered the fortune of a sage's rise; he gathered righteous warriors and rallied allied leagues—with one move he extinguished his foes, with a second journey he set the imperial house aright.
translations.idiomatic: When the times called for talent he answered the opening of a sage's age, gathering loyal fighters and forging alliances—one stroke destroyed his enemies, the next restored the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是內詢帷幄，外仗材雄，推至誠以待人，弘大順以訓物。

translations.literal: Thereupon within he consulted the strategists' tent, without he relied on heroic material; he extended utmost sincerity in treating people and spread great accord to instruct things.
translations.idiomatic: Within he plotted strategy; without he leaned on able men. He treated others with complete sincerity and governed through the great principle of yielding to the cosmic order.

sentences.zh: 高氏籍甲兵之衆，恃戎馬之強，屢入近畿，志圖吞噬。

translations.literal: The Gao clan relied on the mass of armored troops, depended on the strength of war-horses, repeatedly entered the near suburbs, and schemed to swallow and devour.
translations.idiomatic: The Gao family commanded armor by the legion and cavalry by the herd, again and again pressing the capital's outskirts, intent on swallowing the realm.

sentences.zh: 及英謀電發，神旆風馳，弘農建城濮之勳，沙苑有昆陽之捷。

translations.literal: When brilliant plans flashed like lightning, divine banners raced like the wind—Hongnong won a Chengpu merit, Shayuan had a Kunyang triumph.
translations.idiomatic: When his plans struck like lightning and his banners swept like wind—Hongnong brought a victory worthy of Chengpu, Shayuan a triumph to match Kunyang.

sentences.zh: 取威定霸，以弱為強。

translations.literal: Taking prestige to fix hegemony, he made the weak into the strong.
translations.idiomatic: He turned weakness into strength and seized hegemony from victory.

sentences.zh: 紹元宗之衰緒，創隆周之景命。

translations.literal: He continued the declining line of the Yuan clan and founded the splendid mandate of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He upheld the fading Yuan imperial line and founded Northern Zhou's radiant mandate.

sentences.zh: 南清江漢，西舉巴蜀，北控沙漠，東據伊瀍。

translations.literal: South he cleared the Yangtze and Han; west he raised Ba and Shu; north he controlled the desert; east he held the Yi and Luo rivers.
translations.idiomatic: South he secured the Yangtze and Han; west he brought in Ba and Shu; north he held the steppes; east he grasped the Yi and Luo basins.

sentences.zh: 乃擯落魏晉，憲章古昔，修六官之廢典，成一代之鴻規。

translations.literal: Then he cast aside Wei and Jin, took law and pattern from antiquity, restored the abandoned canon of the six offices, and completed the great norm of an age.
translations.idiomatic: He discarded Wei and Jin precedent, looked back to antiquity, revived the six ministries' lost statutes, and finished an institutional order for the age.

sentences.zh: 德刑並用，勳賢兼敘，遠安邇悅，俗阜民和。

translations.literal: Virtue and punishment were both employed; merit and worth were jointly recorded; the distant were settled and the near pleased, customs were rich and the people harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: He wielded both reward and punishment, honored merit and talent, soothed far borders and pleased those near home, and lifted custom until the people flourished in peace.

sentences.zh: 億兆之望有歸，揖讓之期允集。

translations.literal: The hopes of hundreds of millions returned to him; the time for yielding the throne was truly gathered.
translations.idiomatic: The people's countless hopes converged on him; the moment for abdication and transfer of the throne was at hand.

sentences.zh: 功業若此，人臣以終。

translations.literal: Achievement like this, for a minister to end his course.
translations.idiomatic: For a subject to end his career with such achievement.

sentences.zh: 盛矣哉！

translations.literal: How magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: What greatness!

sentences.zh: 非夫雄略冠時，英姿不世，天與神授，緯武經文者，孰能與於此乎。

translations.literal: If not one whose heroic strategy topped the age, whose heroic bearing was not of this generation, whom Heaven and the spirits endowed, who wove martial and civil arts together—who could reach this.
translations.idiomatic: Unless a man's strategy outshone his age, his presence was unmatched in his lifetime, Heaven and the spirits had marked him, and civil and military gifts were woven in one person—who could have done this.

sentences.zh: 昔者，漢獻蒙塵，曹公成夾輔之業；

translations.literal: In former times Han Xian suffered the dust of exile; Duke Cao accomplished the service of supporting from both sides;
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Emperor Xian of Han wandered in humiliation while Cao Cao built the work of a royal champion;

sentences.zh: 晉安播蕩，宋武建匡合之勳。

translations.literal: Jin An was tossed in disorder; Song Wu established the merit of restoring unity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An of Jin was tossed by rebellion while Liu Yu of Song forged the achievement of reunifying the realm.

sentences.zh: 校德論功，綽有餘裕。

translations.literal: Comparing virtue and weighing achievement, he had more than enough to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against them in virtue or deed, he had merit to spare.

sentences.zh: 至於渚宮制勝，闔城孥戮；

translations.literal: As for the victory at Zhugong, the slaughter of the entire city including wives and children;
translations.idiomatic: Yet at Zhugong, where victory meant that an entire city—women and children included—was put to the sword;

sentences.zh: 茹茹歸命，盡種誅夷：雖事出於權道，而用乖於德教。

translations.literal: when the Rouran submitted and the whole seed was exterminated and killed: although the matter issued from expedient policy, the application was at odds with moral teaching.
translations.idiomatic: and when the Rouran surrendered only to have every clan exterminated—acts born perhaps of necessity, yet far from humane governance.

sentences.zh: 周祚之不永，或此之由乎。

translations.literal: That the Zhou fortune was not long—perhaps this was the reason.
translations.idiomatic: That the Zhou dynasty proved so brief may well have begun here.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971, as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou (November 1971).
